This module has three chapters.

1. [Introduction to Survival Analysis](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd)
defines the basic quantities for time-to-event data:
[right censoring](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd#def-right-censor),
the [survival function](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd#def-surv-fn),
the [hazard function](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd#def-hazard),
and the [cumulative hazard](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd#def-cuhaz).
It then covers nonparametric methods:
the [Kaplan-Meier estimator](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd#def-KM-estimator),
the [log-rank test](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd#def-logrank-test),
and the [Nelson-Aalen estimator](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd#def-na-cuhaz-est).

2. [Proportional Hazards Models](proportional-hazards-models.qmd)
introduces the [Cox proportional hazards model](proportional-hazards-models.qmd#def-ph-model),
which relates [covariates](Intro-to-GLMs.qmd#def-predictors) to a
[baseline hazard](proportional-hazards-models.qmd#def-base-hazard)
through [hazard ratios](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd#def-hazard-ratio),
and estimates its coefficients using the
[partial likelihood](proportional-hazards-models.qmd#def-ph-partial-lik).
It also introduces [competing risks](proportional-hazards-models.qmd#def-competing-risks).

3. [Parametric Survival Models](parametric-survival-models.qmd)
assumes a specific distributional family for the event times,
such as the [exponential regression model](parametric-survival-models.qmd#def-exp-reg)
and the [Weibull distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-weibull),
and introduces [accelerated failure time models](parametric-survival-models.qmd#def-aft).
